Intro: Caring for a Maltese’s long, silky coat takes a gentle routine and the right tools to prevent tangles and mats. The steps below walk you from pre-bath prep through blow-drying and finishing touches with realistic time expectations.

1) Pre-brush and inspection (10–20 minutes)
- Use a wide-tooth stainless-steel comb and a pin brush or slicker brush to gently remove loose hair, surface tangles, and debris before the bath. Work in sections, holding the hair near the skin to avoid pulling. Check ears, armpits, behind the ears, and the tail for hidden mats and note any sensitive spots.

2) Gather the correct products and tools (5–10 minutes)
- Essentials: dog-formulated, pH-balanced shampoo (moisturizing or oatmeal if dry skin; whitening/brightening formula for white coats if needed), a conditioner or deep conditioning mask, and a leave-in detangler/conditioning spray.
- Tools: slicker brush, pin brush, stainless-steel comb (wide and fine teeth), dematting rake or mat splitter (for stubborn mats), microfiber towels, non-slip mat, high-velocity or low-heat force dryer, grooming scissors (rounded tip) and thinning shears, nail clippers, cotton balls for ears.
- Extras: ear-cleaning solution, hypoallergenic wipes, and treats to keep your dog calm.

3) Detangle problem areas before wetting (5–15 minutes)
- Apply a small amount of leave-in detangler or conditioning spray to stubborn areas (legs, behind ears, under collar). Gently work out mats from the tips inward using your fingers and a comb or dematting tool; cut out only irreducible mats with blunt-tipped scissors as a last resort. Wet hair makes mats worse, so finish detangling first.

4) Prepare the bathing area and water temperature (2–5 minutes)
- Use a sink or tub with a non-slip mat. Have all items within reach. Run lukewarm (not hot) water and use a cup or sprayer for even wetting. Keep cotton in the ear canals if your Maltese dislikes water getting in the ears (remove afterward and clean ears properly).

5) Shampooing (8–15 minutes)
- Wet coat thoroughly from neck down, avoiding direct spray into eyes/ears. Apply a small amount of dog-formulated shampoo, lather gently from skin outward—Maltese have fine hair so be gentle and thorough. Use a whitening shampoo sparingly if desired (follow directions; do not overuse). Rinse thoroughly until water runs clear to remove all shampoo residue (important to prevent tangles).

6) Conditioning and rinse (5–10 minutes)
- Apply a rinse-out conditioner or a hydrating mask, concentrating on mid-lengths and ends where tangles form. Leave on for the recommended time (usually 1–5 minutes) to restore slip, then rinse completely. For extra manageability, you can use a deep conditioner once a month.

7) Towel blot and apply leave-in conditioner/detangler (5–10 minutes)
- Gently press excess water out with a microfiber towel—do not rub vigorously. While damp, spray a light leave-in conditioner/detangler and comb through with a wide-tooth comb to distribute product evenly. This adds slip for easier drying and reduces static.

8) Blow-dry while brushing (20–45 minutes depending on coat length)
- Use a high-velocity dryer set to warm/low heat or a pet-specific blow dryer on a low setting. Hold the dryer at a safe distance and continuously move it; avoid prolonged heat on one spot. Use a slicker brush or pin brush to brush the coat in the direction of growth while drying to keep hair straight, untangled, and smooth. Work in small sections and finish with a fine-tooth comb to check for missed tangles. For very nervous dogs, use lower airflow and a gentler technique.

9) Finishing trim and coat care (5–15 minutes)
- Once fully dry, perform light trimming around the eyes, paws, sanitary areas, and feathering if desired using rounded-tip scissors. Use thinning shears for a natural finish if needed. Give a final brush-through and apply a small amount of coat polish or light finishing spray (product labeled safe for dogs) to add shine and reduce static.

10) Post-groom routine and prevention (5–10 minutes daily maintenance)
- Expect the entire bathing-to-finish process to take about 45–90 minutes depending on coat length and drying equipment. To keep mats from returning: brush daily (5–10 minutes), use a leave-in detangler after brushing, keep feathering trimmed if you prefer lower maintenance, and bathe every 2–4 weeks (or as your groomer/vet recommends). Reward your Maltese with treats and check ears and paws regularly.

Conclusion: With consistent detangling, the right conditioning products, and a careful blow-dry routine, a Maltese’s coat stays silky, matt-free, and healthy. Regular short brushing sessions are the key to reducing full grooming time and preventing painful mats.
